---
title: "Limits"
subtitle: "What is wrong with this model, in the order it matters"
---

::: {.caveat}
Every number on this site comes from a model whose behavioural coefficients are not fitted
to observation. The physics is real; the trajectory is structural, not predictive.
:::

## 1. The dominant coefficients are unfitted

Morris screening puts `p_cap` (annual purchase hazard ceiling) and `b0` (baseline
propensity) at the top of every output. Neither is a measured quantity. Until they are
calibrated against AC ownership by income band, room-AC sales trends and licensee summer
load growth, the level of the trajectory is a choice, not a finding. The *shape* — who
adopts first, where waste heat concentrates, how fabric and income interact — is far more
robust than the level.

## 2. ΔT is a uniform city-mean increment

The feedback uses a scalar transfer coefficient applied equally to every hour and every
ward. Real AC waste heat concentrates at night and in dense areas: published coupled
simulations find little daytime effect and roughly 0.6–1.5 °C of night-time warming where
cooling is widespread. This model therefore understates night warming in adopting wards and
overstates daytime warming everywhere. Replacing $k$ with SUEWS or PALM-4U per local
climate zone is the single largest physics upgrade available.

## 3. Placeholder building parameters

Energy use intensities, appliance stocks, U-values, air change rates, thermal capacitance
and roof solar gains are all plausible values chosen by hand. No Indian archetype library
is used. The model was tuned once against city peak electricity (~4,000 MW across the four
licensees) and left there; further tuning without measured data would be fitting noise.

## 4. Input data limits

**Heights** carry 1.5–9 m error, propagating into floor counts, floor area, capacitance and
household counts. **Typology** is roughly 35% evidence-supported; the remainder comes from a
size-and-height heuristic. **The slum layer is 2016** and sets archetype, thermal properties
and income band simultaneously, so its vintage propagates into all three — Mumbai's informal
stock has changed since, particularly where redevelopment has occurred. **The income proxy
is land value.**

## 5. Physics simplifications

- **COP fixed at 3.0.** Real COP degrades as ambient temperature rises, so cooling energy
  and waste heat are understated exactly when they matter most.
- **All condenser heat treated as sensible.** Commercial cooling towers reject mostly latent
  heat; in a coastal, humid city that distinction changes the surface energy balance.
- **Vehicle heat rests on one invented number** — city-wide daily vehicle-kilometres — yet
  contributes a large share of total Q~f~. It is the least constrained term in the model.
- **Solar gain is a flat clear-sky proxy** with no shading, orientation or sky view factor.

## 6. Structural omissions

- **The stock is frozen to 2040**: no redevelopment, no new construction, no population
  growth. Over fifteen years Mumbai's redevelopment pipeline probably changes cooling demand
  more than adoption behaviour does.
- **No daytime population redistribution.** Metabolic heat sits at people's homes all day,
  understating Q~f~ in BKC, Nariman Point and Lower Parel during working hours and
  overstating it in the suburbs.
- **No tenure split.** Renters cannot install, landlords do not pay bills; the split-incentive
  problem is large in Mumbai's rental and chawl stock.
- **No tariff slabs.** Maharashtra residential tariffs telescope steeply, so crossing a slab
  sharply raises marginal cost. Electricity price does not enter the decision at all.
- **No replacement cycle.** Units are bought and never retired, so efficiency standards
  cannot be tested.
- **Commercial and industrial cooling is exogenous** — a fixed fraction per archetype — despite
  being 43% of modelled energy.

## 7. What is *not* a limitation

**Stochastic uncertainty.** With 3.2 million households, seed variance in 2040 penetration
is under 0.1 percentage points. Presenting replicate ensembles as uncertainty quantification
would be misleading; the uncertainty is in the coefficients.
